title: AIIMS Principles and Concepts

nodes.text: Introduction to AIIMS Principles and Concepts
Flexibility: AIIMS must be adaptable to an all hazards-all agency environment

evidence.source_text: 1. Flexibility AIIMS be adaptable to an all hazards-all agency environment.

nodes.text: Management by Objectives: Incident Controller determines desired outcomes

evidence.source_text: 2. Management by Objectives A process of management where the Incident Controller, consulting as appropriate with the Incident Management Team and supporting agencies, determines the desired outcomes of the incident.

nodes.text: Functional Management: Structure organization into sections based on work type

evidence.source_text: 3. Functional Management The process of structuring an organisation into sections or units based on the type of work to be performed.

nodes.text: Span of Control: Apply principle in structuring and staffing Incident Management Team

evidence.source_text: 4. Span of Control A principle that needs to be applied in both the structuring and staffing of an Incident Management Team.

nodes.text: Unity of Command: One set of common objectives for all responders

evidence.source_text: 5. Unity of Command There is one set of common objectives for all those involved in the response to an incident.

nodes.text: Adaptability and Scalability: Incident Management Team size reflects incident complexity

evidence.source_text: Adaptability and Scalability  The size and structure of the Incident Management Team should reflect the size and complexity of the incident.

nodes.text: Uniform Terminology: Agreed terminology for effective communication

evidence.source_text: Uniform Terminology  If all agencies are to apply the System there needs to be agreed terminology and definitions.

nodes.text: Defined Management Structure: Clearly defined and agreed management structure

evidence.source_text: Defined Management Structure  In adopting a functional management model, there needs to be a clearly defined and agreed management structure.

nodes.text: Common Operating Picture: Shared understanding of the incident

evidence.source_text: Common Operating Picture  A description of the shared and consistent understanding the Incident Management Team has of the incident.

nodes.text: Clearly Defined Roles and Responsibilities: Agreed responsibilities for all roles

evidence.source_text: Clearly Defined Roles and Responsibilities  In defining the management structure, there needs to be a set of clearly defined and agreed responsibilities for all who are appointed to a role.

nodes.text: Clearly Defined Information Flows: Clear reporting relationships and communication

evidence.source_text: Clearly Defined Information Flows  For a functional management structure to operate effectively, it needs to be clear what reporting relationships exist.

nodes.text: Understanding of AIIMS Principles and Concepts complete

evidence.source_text: An understanding of these concepts is essential to the effective application of the System.
